cost_asymmetry.basis: ILLUSTRATIVE PLACEHOLDER, NOT AN OPERATOR STATEMENT. $60/idle vehicle-revenue-hour is the order of magnitude of publicly reported US demand-response operating cost per revenue hour; $75/unserved trip is a stand-in for an operator's own valuation of denying a legally-entitled ADA trip (complaint handling, FTA exposure, and the policy weight placed on the denial itself), which no public dataset records. Any real deployment MUST replace both numbers with the operator's stated values -- the resulting service level moves directly with them.

limitations: Public panels record DELIVERED service (trips carried, vehicle-hours operated), never DENIED trips. Realised ridership is demand censored from above by the capacity actually run, so under-provisioning -- the failure this cost asymmetry exists to price -- is unobservable in it. Any accuracy figure computed against such a panel is a claim about reproducing an operator's past commitment, not about meeting rider need. Closing this gap requires consented operator denial / unmet-trip records; until then no capacity result here can reach Validated.
The cost asymmetry is an illustrative placeholder, not an operator statement. The critical ratio, and therefore every capacity number here, moves directly with it.
Productivity is a per-series point estimate (median historical trips/VRH); its own variation is measured and reported but not propagated into the service level.

The forecasters are deliberately simple and fit-free (seasonal naive, YoY-adjusted seasonal naive). This is a test of the CAPACITY DECISION LAYER, not a claim that these are the best available demand models.
Monthly agency grain. Nothing here demonstrates capacity planning at the hour-of-day grain a dispatcher works at.

panel_level_drift.reason: 5 of 5 monitored feature(s) drifted (PSI >= 0.2 or KS p < 0.01): lag12, lag1, roll3, yoy_ratio, month.
